title: Orbit-stable extension-obstruction atlas for lifting 42-vertex frontier colorings
novelty_claim: The missing Ramsey object is a reusable dictionary of minimal obstruction cores that explain why many nonisomorphic 42-vertex critical colorings fail to extend to 43 vertices. If those cores recur across parent families, they become a new structural bridge between lower-bound search and upper-bound impossibility proofs rather than another optimizer variant.
closest_prior_art: Study of Exoo's Lower Bound for Ramsey number R(5,5) (Ge et al., 2022)
Can genetic algorithms with the symmetric heuristic find the Ramsey number R(5,5) (2010)
Angeltveit-McKay upper-bound line on R(5,5), including R(5,5) <= 48 and the later <= 46 case-checking line
differentiation: This direction does not claim novelty from better search, better SAT, or lower defect scores. Its claim is that failed one-vertex extensions share orbit-stable minimal obstructions that transfer across held-out parent families and can be reused as sound pruning lemmas or proof artifacts.
easiest_falsifier: Enumerate orbit-distinct one-vertex extensions from diverse 42-vertex parents. If the minimal obstruction witnesses do not recur, do not transfer under leave-one-parent-out evaluation, or fail witness-survival checks when used as filters, kill the hypothesis.
evidence_plan: Build a canonical atlas of known 42-vertex frontier graphs; classify inequivalent one-vertex extensions and their failure types; cluster recurring obstruction cores; test transfer across held-out parent families; audit soundness against all known witnesses; measure whether the cores compress search or proof state better than raw extension tables.
budget_envelope: Primary budget only. During synthesis, spec and benchmark design only. After approval, run one champion pilot focused on recurrence and transfer before funding any broader search.

title: Decomposition-primitive upgrade beyond split-vertex and transverse-edge gluing
novelty_claim: The upper-bound bottleneck may be the decomposition language itself rather than the solver layer. Orbit-balanced two-vertex or shell-based decompositions could collapse the exact residue in a way that the current one-vertex split plus gluing pipeline cannot.
closest_prior_art: A new upper bound on the Ramsey number R(5,5) (McKay and Radziszowski, 1992)
The later Angeltveit-McKay R(5,5) <= 46 case-checking line
Gauthier's 2025 upper-bound strategy based on splitting vertices and transverse-edge gluing
differentiation: The novelty claim is about changing the proof object and case partition, not about importing a stronger SAT engine. Success must appear as a smaller verified residue, smaller proof footprint, or faster checker runtime under matched solver conditions.
easiest_falsifier: Benchmark the candidate primitives on solved subcases and representative 45-vertex residues under the same solver and proof-logging setup. If they do not outperform the split/gluing baseline on residue size or checked proof cost, kill the hypothesis.
evidence_plan: Predefine candidate primitives such as adjacent-pair, nonadjacent-pair, forced-K4 shell, independent-4 shell, and equitable orbit partitions; compare them against the current baseline on unknown-edge count, isomorphism collapse, residue size, proof bytes, and checker runtime.
budget_envelope: Backup budget only. Do not open this track until the champion is killed or explicitly deprioritized. When opened, fund one matched benchmark ladder and no solver-shopping.

title: Proof-carrying reusable obstruction certificates from failed exact branches
novelty_claim: Exact R(5,5) computation can become cumulative if failed branches yield canonical, orbit-stable obstruction certificates that transfer across later branches instead of serving only as one-off proof logs.
closest_prior_art: Schur Number Five proof-logging and certificate practice
SAT+CAS verified Ramsey certificates for nearby exact problems
differentiation: This is not generic proof logging. The claim is that the extracted cores survive changes of branch, symmetry representative, and subfamily, so they behave like reusable forbidden-partial-coloring lemmas rather than archived solver debris.
easiest_falsifier: Extract canonical cores on a verified benchmark ladder and test them on held-out branch families. If transfer is weak, encoding-specific, or increases checked proof cost more than it prunes, kill the hypothesis or fold it into infrastructure.
evidence_plan: Use small verified cases and tractable R(5,5) subcases to define canonicalization, transfer tests, and proof-size accounting; measure prune rate, proof bytes, checker runtime, and invariance across symmetry conventions.
budget_envelope: Reserve only. Fund only as an attachment to H1 or H2, never as a standalone first-line direction.
